given: a stock table with existing rows whose batch_number and serial_number were backfilled before the drop
then: every existing stock row survives with its batch_number, serial_number, and location values intact; the row count is unchanged and no row is dropped or corrupted

independence.rationale: AC1 only asserts the inventory_code column is gone from the schema shape; a drop could succeed on the schema yet lose or corrupt rows. This AC is the separately-breakable data-durability outcome (R1) — rows and their retained values survive the drop — and can fail while AC1 passes, and vice versa.

architectural_notes: Infra-layer data-durability contract on the stock table, realized by the same Alembic drop migration run atomically against the paired branch. The drop must be a pure column removal that never DELETEs or mutates the surviving location/batch_number/serial_number values, so verification is a before/after row-count and value diff on the real branch (PI3 atomicity, PI4 row preservation), owned by the migrations module rather than app/services. Cross-cutting concern: R1 data preservation across schema change — enforced at the DB layer and proven by a real-branch integration test, never an in-memory substitute.
